title: Rejection audit: separate generic product curation from elder-specific latent-asset friction
purpose: Use failure/rejection evidence to determine whether value-form routing is a unique intergenerational missing edge or mostly ordinary product/market curation, and isolate any genuinely elder-specific upstream friction that survives.
truth_rules: GENERIC PRODUCT-MARKET FIT != UNIQUE INTERGENERATIONAL EDGE
SOURCE-SIDE LEGIBILITY MAY PRECEDE NORMAL MARKET MECHANISMS

rejection_evidence.fact: A 2026 community handcraft study reports 83.3% of community workers saying there is no fixed sales point; products are often sold only at occasional holiday stalls.
rejection_evidence.interpretation: An otherwise usable capability can remain non-economic simply because there is no durable route to buyers.

rejection_evidence.fact: The same study reports material, thread and packaging costs while low-price selling produces too little surplus even to subsidize class materials.
rejection_evidence.interpretation: Emotional/cultural value does not automatically produce margin.

rejection_evidence.fact: Community staff report that the personal therapeutic/story context behind each elder-made item is rarely surfaced, making it difficult to stimulate purchase interest.
rejection_evidence.interpretation: The raw object alone may not expose the value that gives it differentiation.

rejection_evidence.fact: Tǎmadrama found that product-only retail did not attract the new mall's surrounding resident customer base; the operator added hands-on classes and livestreaming.
rejection_evidence.interpretation: A translated asset can fail because its form/channel fit is wrong, even when the underlying capability is viable.

rejection_evidence.fact: Fengtai discovered 40+ capable older residents, appointed a smaller core group, and planned professional deep development for selected works rather than developing every discovered asset.
rejection_evidence.interpretation: The system already behaves as if only a subset of latent assets deserves deeper translation investment.

adjacent_selection_criteria.fact: Shanghai's 2026 silver-economy innovation competition evaluates technical maturity, IP, industrialization prospects, business-model feasibility, market fit, usability/user experience and real-scene matching.
adjacent_selection_criteria.evidence_role: adjacent market-selection benchmark, not direct elder-asset evidence

reasoning: The observed rejection criteria substantially overlap ordinary product management, merchandising and market-validation criteria.
Existing designers, retail operators, social enterprises and channel partners already perform these functions.
The presence of older actors changes source material but does not by itself create a new routing science.
Therefore generalized 'value-form routing' is not currently supported as a distinctive missing edge.

elder_specific_upstream_friction.label: LATENT HUMAN-ASSET LEGIBILITY / ACTIVATION
elder_specific_upstream_friction.statement: Before ordinary product/market mechanisms can work, many older-adult assets are not visible or legible as assets at all. They may exist only as habits, memories, tacit know-how, hobbies, local relationships, teaching ability or unpriced craft inside a person's everyday life.

observed_indicators.fact: Fengtai had to conduct community-level mapping to discover 40+ older residents with capabilities; the program describes these capabilities as scattered/hidden in communities.
Beijing Silver Artisan explicitly frames the problem as older artisans being hidden and unknown until a social-service operator discovers and activates them.
Fudan's memoir process requires trained interviewing, background research and narrative elicitation because life-history value is fragmented and embodied rather than already packaged as a product.

Hangzhou's AI-Skill pilot requires older adults to externalize accumulated cooking/family-education experience into structured callable form, showing the source knowledge is initially embodied and not machine-callable.

possible_functions: discover capability that the person may not name as an asset
elicit/observe tacit knowledge or practical skill
separate personal meaning from transferable utility
make the asset legible enough for ordinary product/market/channel mechanisms to evaluate it
triage: translate / preserve / market / teach / ignore

deeper_causal_model.after: EMBODIED / INVISIBLE OLDER-ASSET → LEGIBILITY / ACTIVATION → then ordinary curation / product-market mechanisms
deeper_causal_model.key_learning: The distinctive intergenerational friction may sit before product-market fit. Markets cannot route what they cannot see, describe, permission or compare.

contradictions: Existing talent databases and community talent pools may already solve obvious/high-signal capabilities.
Many ordinary older adults may not hold transferable assets worth activating.
Asset discovery can become expensive qualitative interviewing with weak hit rate.
AI may increasingly help older people self-externalize their own knowledge, reducing the need for a human discovery layer.
Communities have privileged trust/access that may be difficult for a private operator to replicate.
The surviving friction may have high social value but insufficient private willingness to pay.
next_action: Audit the source-side discovery/legibility layer. Search how programs actually find hidden older capabilities: self-nomination vs door-to-door/community mapping vs referrals; hit/selection rates; what kinds of capabilities remain invisible to talent databases; whether one activated elder refers others; and whether current silver-talent databases only capture explicit professional credentials while missing everyday/tacit assets. Kill the line if discovery is too labor-intensive, low-yield, or already normalized by community/talent systems.
